lines.text: Why are America and Iran always fighting?
It all started with oil.
Iran sits on some of the largest oil reserves on Earth.
But in the early nineteen fifties, a British company controlled it,
and Iran got only about sixteen percent of the profits.
In nineteen fifty-one, Iran's democratically elected prime minister,
Mohammad Mossadegh, nationalized the oil.
Britain was furious.
So in nineteen fifty-three, the CIA and British intelligence ran Operation Ajax
and overthrew him.
They put the Shah, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, back in full power.
He ruled for twenty-six years,
and American companies got a forty percent share of Iran's oil.
But his secret police tortured opponents and crushed dissent.
In nineteen seventy-nine, Iranians rose up.
The Shah fled,
and Ayatollah Khomeini took power.
When the Shah was let into the US, Iranian students stormed the American embassy
and held fifty-two Americans hostage
for four hundred and forty-four days.
They feared another coup.
Then in nineteen eighty, Saddam Hussein's Iraq invaded Iran,
and over time the US backed Iraq with intelligence.
Hundreds of thousands died.
Iran answered by funding groups like Hezbollah and Hamas,
and building a nuclear program.
America answered with sanctions.
In twenty fifteen, Obama's deal lifted sanctions
in exchange for strict nuclear limits.
Trump tore it up in twenty eighteen, calling it the worst deal ever.
In his second term, talks failed, sanctions returned,
and the US and Israel struck Iran directly.
Seventy years of oil, coups and revenge.
And it's still not over.
If you want updates related to geopolitics,
then make sure to follow our page, Things Explained.
